R1's preventable-not-recoverable rests on 2 studies, both non-channel (a kinase, a ligase), and is contested by R1's own table (adult restoration of a synaptic regulator eliminated interictal spiking in the same animals) and by two sources neither producer read (antisense reactivation of the same ligase locus rescued audiogenic susceptibility at P21 and the electroencephalographic rhythm phenotype in juveniles and adults, with improvement correlated to protein level). corrected_wording: Post-onset restoration has recovered a spontaneous convulsive seizure endpoint in two models, both channel or channel-transcript lesions. In non-channel genes the result splits by endpoint identity and restoration mode rather than by gene class: conditional re-expression left epileptic spasms and audiogenic susceptibility unmoved in two models, while adult conditional re-expression abolished interictal spiking in one and antisense reactivation of one of the same loci rescued audiogenic susceptibility at P21 and the electroencephalographic rhythm phenotype in adults. Two studies support each side as framed, and with the antisense studies the same gene appears on both sides. Gene class is correlated with the split, not established as its cause; the factor that tracks outcome across all of them is the level and distribution of restoration achieved together with whether the endpoint is continuously generated excitability or a developmentally built seizure phenotype. WWOX, a WW-domain oxidoreductase-domain adaptor with no channel function, falls on the non-channel side; its carried endpoint, spike-wave discharge rate, is an interictal network measure, the one sub-class in which a non-channel gene has recovered after onset, so the external precedent for it is split rather than negative.
